title: Candles, “witches,” anyone had a similar mallworld dream?
content: I have reoccurring dreams at malls and all kinds of other places, but I never made the connection to this childhood dream I had, even though it’s always been significant to me. I think I was in middle school when I had this dream. It starts with me waking up in a simple, small mall. All the stores are closed but the main lights are on. There are other people all around except they’re all asleep on the floor (and they’re all my age, middle school age). We all have candles and a dish to carry them on, but my candle is the only one that’s lit. I go up to one of the people sleeping on the floor, touch the wick of their candle, and ignite it. This allows them to wake up. Apparently, I’m the only one who can ignite people’s candles and wake them up, so I go around doing it for everyone. We all fell asleep because there are three old women in the mall with the power to extinguish our candles—or put us to sleep forever (we called them witches)—and for some reason they did this to us before the events of the dream. We realize we have to get rid of these women if we’re ever going to be safe, or at least that’s my perspective and I get everyone to agree with me (lol). We gather into a crowd and go confront the women. When we reach the room they’re in I verbally confront them, asking why they would do this or something similar. The woman closest to me smiles and blows my candle out which wakes me up. Thoughts or similar experiences? Some days ago I made a comment on someone’s post about how something like mallworld could be humanity’s trigger into things like mass lucid dreaming, and I made a connection to this dream. Symbolically, I think the candles could represent something like that, people becoming “aware” (that experiences like this are part of our reality). Maybe over time if more people become interested in topics like this and lucid dreaming, or similar topics, it could lead to cool discoveries! The three old women reminded me of the three fates. They also seem to represent oppression and hierarchy with the age and power difference between us and them.
